implementation_statement: POL-02 (P06) was approved 2026-09-04 and covers IT and OT. OT account procedures (SCADA, jump host, relays) are due 2026-11-30.

Corporate and cloud accounts are created in the identity provider from HR tickets. OT domain accounts are created by the SCADA/OT Administrator on a manager's email. Gap: the 6 HMI consoles use shared operator accounts, SCADA administrator accounts have never been reviewed, and the jump host has one shared vendor account.
evidence: OT domain user export; jump host account list

implementation_statement: SCADA enforces operator, engineer, and administrator roles for control actions. OMS roles separate dispatchers, crews, and viewers.
evidence: SCADA role table; OMS role matrix

implementation_statement: An OT DMZ exists for the jump host, historian replica, and integration server. Gap: 14 legacy any rules on the IT/OT firewall let OMS and historian traffic bypass the DMZ.
Operators cannot change SCADA database points. Gap: 5 engineers hold SCADA administrator rights they use only for display edits.

The identity provider and the OT domain lock accounts after 10 failed attempts. HMI operator sessions are tailored out of lockout so an operator is never locked out during an event; DCC physical access compensates.

Engineering workstations and corporate endpoints lock after 10 minutes. HMI consoles are tailored out (SP 800-82 Rev. 3 recognizes that locking operator consoles can harm operations); the DCC is badge-controlled and staffed 24x7.

Remote access to OT goes only through the jump host in the OT DMZ. Gap: the SCADA vendor and the relay testing contractor share a standing account with no MFA, and the corporate VPN uses passwords only.

implementation_statement: No wireless networks in the DCC or substation control houses. Wireless on relays and gateways is disabled (verified at Substation N and Substation E on 2026-07-28).
Awareness and training rules are in POL-05 (P06). Training procedures for field and DCC staff are due 2026-12-31.
All staff complete the annual CIP awareness module (last 2026-03). Office staff also get phishing exercises. Gap: field and DCC staff get no phishing training.
System operators are trained on SCADA operation by the vendor. Gap: no role-based training on recognizing and reporting OT cyber events.
SCADA logs operator commands and alarms; the jump host and gateways log sessions. Gap: event types to log are not defined, and gateway logs stay on the device.
SCADA records time, point, command, and console. Gap: shared operator accounts mean records do not identify the person.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: No review of SCADA, jump host, or gateway logs today. Weekly review from the log workspace is planned with the OT monitoring project (2027-03-31).
GPS clocks at the DCC and at the BES substations provide time to SCADA, relays, and gateways.
Logs are stored only on the systems that create them. Forwarding to the write-protected log workspace is planned.
CIP evidence must be kept 3 calendar years (CIP-003-9 Compliance 1.2). Gap: jump host logs roll after 30 days and evidence is scattered.
Audit generation is on for SCADA and the jump host; off on the historian and 9 substation gateways.
Independent control assessment performed 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-14 (P07).
Interconnection and operating agreements exist with the transmission owner. Gap: no written data exchange terms with the AMI and CIS vendors.
All weaknesses from P07 are tracked in the POA&M with owners and dates.
Continuous monitoring strategy planned with the OT monitoring project; monthly POA&M review starts 2026-10.
SCADA vendor build documents exist. Gap: no current baseline for substation gateways and relays (firmware and settings versions).
No change records for relay setting or gateway access list changes. A two-person review and change record is planned (2026-12-31).
Relay setting changes need the relay password, held by protection staff. Gap: the relay testing contractor also knows the passwords.
SCADA servers follow the vendor hardening guide. Gap: the Substation E gateway access list was left open after commissioning (P07 finding, corrected 2026-08-13).
Unused services are disabled on SCADA servers. Gap: HMIs allow USB storage.
SCADA servers and HMIs are inventoried. Gap: substation gateways, radios, and relay firmware versions are not.
The storm restoration plan covers operations. A cyber recovery procedure for SCADA is due 2026-12-31.
The storm restoration plan and backup DCC procedure exist. Gap: they do not cover loss of SCADA to a cyber event or recovery order (P05).
No SCADA restore test has been performed; failover to the backup DCC last tested 2023. Quarterly restore tests from 2026-12 and annual failover before June 1 are planned.
Backups go to the standby server at the backup DCC (a separate site). Gap: same OT network and credentials; no offline copy.
The backup DCC at the North operations center can run SCADA from the standby server. Gap: failover untested since 2023.
Company fiber, licensed radio, and private cellular reach the substations. Gap: crews depend on commercial cellular for OMS mobile.
SCADA database backups run nightly; OMS and GIS back up daily to a separate cloud backup account. Gap: SCADA backups are not offline or immutable and have never been restored.
Vendor rebuild media are on hand. Gap: no documented rebuild sequence or time estimate.
Identification rules are in POL-02. OT procedures due 2026-11-30.
Unique accounts in the identity provider and OT domain. Gap: shared HMI operator accounts and the shared vendor account.
MFA for privileged cloud and SaaS accounts. Gap: no MFA for OT domain administrators or the jump host.

implementation_statement: MFA for email, CIS, and OMS users. Gap: the legacy VPN uses passwords only (36 users).
Identifiers come from HR records; OT identifiers follow the same naming. Identifiers are not reused.
Password rules are enforced in the identity provider and the OT domain. Gap: relay passwords are shared with the contractor and changed only yearly.
POL-03 (P06) approved 2026-09-04 covers IT and OT incidents and the low impact plan duties.
Incident response training for DCC and protection staff planned with the tabletop (2026-10-30).
The low impact plan was last tested by tabletop on 2023-06-14, so the 36-month test due by 2026-06-14 was missed. A tabletop of a Reportable Cyber Security Incident is scheduled for 2026-10-20.
The low impact Cyber Security Incident response plan (2022) and the P08 OT runbook (approved 2026-09-04) define handling. Gap: untested; no OT forensic support arranged.
IT incidents are tracked in the ticketing system. OT events are recorded only in the DCC operator log.

The EOP-004-4 Operating Plan covers DOE-417 and NERC event reports. Gap: E-ISAC notification for Reportable Cyber Security Incidents and DOE-417 cyber criteria were missing from the IT plan (added in P08).

implementation_statement: The low impact plan and the P08 runbook form the incident response plan. Update within 180 days after a test is required (Att. 1 Sec. 4.6).
Protection System maintenance follows the PRC-005 program; test records are kept for each relay.
Vendor remote maintenance goes through the jump host. Gap: standing access; no approval or session monitoring.
Retired drives are wiped or shredded by a certified vendor with certificates.
USB drives are used for SCADA and relay file transfers without scanning. Scanning kiosks are planned (2026-12-31).
The HR Manager and the Manager of Engineering and Protection approve substation access. Gap: control house keys are not tracked.
Substations are fenced and locked; the DCC uses badge access. Gap: 3 keys held by former employees were never recovered.
Control house door alarms report to the DCC; operators dispatch a crew or law enforcement.
The P06 policy set was approved 2026-09-04 with annual review. The CIP low impact policy is reviewed at least every 15 calendar months.
This SSP documents the DOP; the CIP low impact cyber security plan is a referenced artifact.
POL-05 acceptable use rules approved 2026-09-04. Acknowledgments for all staff due 2026-10-31.

The IT Manager is the Information Security Lead; the VP of Operations is the CIP Senior Manager (R3 record).

implementation_statement: Risk tolerance and acceptance authority are set in POL-01 and P01.
Background checks for all hires, including DCC and protection staff.
Accounts are disabled on the last day. Gap: key return is not part of the exit checklist.
Contractors sign confidentiality terms. Gap: no security requirements for contractor laptops or remote access.
FIPS 199 categorization in section 6 of this plan; CIP-002 impact rating in the categorization record of 2025-11-18.
2026 risk assessment per SP 800-30 (P01).
No OT vulnerability review. Quarterly review of vendor bulletins and CISA ICS advisories against the inventory, plus passive scanning, is planned (2026-12-31).
Procurement templates have no security terms. OT and SaaS contract terms are due at each renewal.
CIS vendor SOC 2 on file; AMI vendor SOC 2 obtained 2026-08 and reviewed (P09). Gap: no security terms for SCADA, OMS, or AMI vendors.
Two HMIs and the historian run an unsupported operating system. Upgrade funded for 2027-03-31.

Firewalls separate corporate, DMZ, SCADA, and substation networks; Substation N gateway permits only the SCADA master and the relay engineering workstation. Gap: legacy any rules at the IT/OT firewall.
Fiber links are private; OMS traffic uses TLS. Gap: DNP3 runs without authentication or encryption over licensed radio and private cellular.
OMS and GIS data are encrypted at rest by the cloud provider.
Corporate endpoints patch monthly. Gap: no OT patch cycle; SCADA patches applied only at vendor upgrades.
Antivirus on SCADA servers and HMIs with monthly signature updates; company relay laptops have antivirus and allowlisting. Gap: contractor laptops unchecked.
No OT security monitoring. Passive monitoring at the DCC and both BES substations is funded (2027-03-31).

implementation_statement: The IT Manager and the SCADA/OT Administrator receive CISA ICS advisories, E-ISAC bulletins, and vendor notices.
Vendor installers are signed. Gap: signatures and hashes are not checked before install.
Records follow the corporate schedule. Gap: no 3-year rule for CIP evidence.
Critical OT products are bought from the original vendors. Gap: no documented supply chain process.
Annual review of key vendors (SOC 2 or questionnaire) planned from 2027.
Hardware is bought from authorized channels. Gap: software integrity not verified (see SI-7).
